snapshot.source: Read-only export of local tracker; account emails redacted and content reviewed for Demo

bugs.title: System allows duplicate project names
bugs.description: The system allows a user to create multiple projects with the same name.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Create a project named "Test Project".
2. Create and submit another project named "Test Project".
bugs.expected_result: The system rejects the second project because a project with that name already exists.
bugs.actual_result: The second project is created successfully.

bugs.title: Textareas contain leading whitespace when creating a new bug
bugs.description: The Description, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Result, and Actual Result textareas contain leading whitespace when the New Bug form is opened.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open a project and click New Bug.
2. Click into the Description field.
3. Repeat for Steps to Reproduce, Expected Result, and Actual Result.
bugs.expected_result: The textareas should be empty when opened, with the placeholder text displayed.
bugs.actual_result: Each textarea initially contains leading whitespace. The placeholder text only appears after the whitespace is deleted.

bugs.title: Bug IDs are not project-specific
bugs.description:
Bug IDs are currently generated globally across all projects. As a result, a new bug in one project can receive an ID that reflects bugs created in other projects.

For example, the AI QA Bug Triage project currently contains BUG-8 and BUG-11 instead of starting its numbering from BUG-1.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Create a project and create several bug reports.
2. Create a second project.
3. Create a bug in the second project.
4. Observe the Bug ID.
bugs.expected_result: Bug IDs should start at BUG-1 for each project and increment independently within that project.
bugs.actual_result: Bug IDs continue from the global bug sequence across all projects.

bugs.title: New project owner can see bugs from a deleted project
bugs.description:
After User A deletes a project, its bugs remain in the database. If a new project created by User B receives the same project ID, User B can see those old bugs.

This exposes one user’s project data to another user.

Environment and investigation evidence: Verified on 9 September 2026 at commit 6069f8c (main), on Windows with Python 3.14.2, FastAPI, SQLite, and FastAPI TestClient. The investigation used a fresh disposable database and two distinct registered users; no real projects were deleted. Project deletion returned HTTP 200. User B’s new project received the deleted project’s ID, and its bug-list response included User A’s original bug. SQLite foreign-key enforcement was disabled. The existing baseline suite passed all 119 tests despite this defect.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
Precondition: Use a fresh disposable test database and two registered users, A and B. Reproduce through the API, using the acting user’s bearer token for each request.

1. As User A, create a project using POST /projects with a valid name. Record its project ID as {project_id}.
2. As User A, create a bug in that project using POST /projects/{project_id}/bugs with a valid title.
3. As User A, delete the project using DELETE /projects/{project_id}.
4. As User B, create a new project using POST /projects with a valid name. Confirm it receives the deleted project’s ID.
5. As User B, retrieve the new project’s bug list using GET /projects/{project_id}/bugs.
bugs.expected_result: User B’s new project has an empty bug list. Bugs from User A’s deleted project are never visible in it.
bugs.actual_result: User B’s new project displays the bug created in User A’s deleted project.

bugs.title: POST /register returns HTTP 500 for passwords over bcrypt's 72-byte limit
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome 153, Swagger UI, local development
bugs.description: Registration accepts a password longer than bcrypt's supported 72-byte limit and passes it to password hashing. This causes an unhandled server error instead of a validation response.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the POST /register endpoint in Swagger UI.
2. Enter a valid email address.
3. Enter a password longer than 72 bytes that otherwise meets password requirements.
4. Submit the request.
bugs.expected_result: POST /register should reject the password with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Content and a validation message.
bugs.actual_result: POST /register returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

bugs.title: Project form feedback remains stale after correction, successful edit, cancel, or reopening
bugs.description:
Project form feedback is not consistently cleared when it is no longer relevant.

The issue affects both Create and Edit project interactions. Validation or success feedback from a previous form state can remain visible after the user corrects the input, successfully saves an edit, cancels, or starts a new project interaction.

This can leave the page showing feedback that no longer matches the current state.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the Projects page.
2. Edit an existing project.
3. Replace the project name with only spaces.
4. Click Save.
5. Enter a valid project name.
6. Click Save again.
7. Observe the feedback message.

Additional reproduction:
8. Trigger either a validation error or successful project creation message.
9. Click Cancel.
10. Open New Project again.
11. Observe the feedback area.
bugs.expected_result:
Project-specific transient feedback should reflect the current form state.

- Project-name validation feedback should clear once the user enters a valid name.
- A successful project edit should not leave an earlier validation error visible.
- Cancel should clear feedback associated with the current form interaction.
- Opening a new Create/Edit interaction should not display stale feedback from the previous interaction.
- Unrelated page-level, network, or authorization errors should not be cleared by project-name input changes.
bugs.actual_result:
Project form feedback can remain visible after it is no longer relevant.

- "Project name is required." remains after the user corrects the project name.
- After correcting an invalid Edit value and successfully saving the project, the old validation message still remains visible.
- Validation or success feedback can remain after clicking Cancel.
- Old feedback can remain visible when opening New Project again.

bugs.title: Project edit accepts whitespace-only project name
bugs.description:
A Project Owner can edit an existing project and save a project name that contains only whitespace characters.

The application should treat a whitespace-only project name as invalid in the same way as an empty project name. Currently, the update is accepted and the project is saved without a meaningful visible name.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in as the Project Owner.
2. Open an existing project.
3. Edit the project name.
4. Replace the name with spaces only, for example "   ".
5. Save the changes.
bugs.expected_result: The update should be rejected because a project name containing only whitespace is not a valid project name.
bugs.actual_result: The project is successfully updated with a whitespace-only name.

bugs.title: No success confirmation is displayed after project creation
bugs.description:
After a project is created successfully, the application adds the new project to the project list but does not display any explicit success confirmation.

The user should receive clear feedback that the project creation completed successfully, for example through a success message or notification.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in.
2. Open the Projects page.
3. Enter a valid project name.
4. Create the project.
bugs.expected_result: The user should receive a clear confirmation that the project was created successfully.
bugs.actual_result: The project is created and appears in the project list, but no explicit success confirmation is displayed.

bugs.title: Removing an assigned project member leaves bugs assigned to that user
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome 153, Desktop, Project Owner account, local development
bugs.description:
When a Project Owner removes a project member who is currently assigned to one or more bugs, the member is removed from the project but their existing bug assignments remain unchanged.

This leaves bugs assigned to a user who is no longer a member of the project. When a project member is removed, any bugs assigned to that user within the project should automatically become unassigned.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in as a Project Owner.
2. Open a project.
3. Add another user to the project as a QA Analyst or Developer.
4. Create or update a bug and assign it to that user.
5. Verify that the user is shown as the bug assignee.
6. Remove the assigned user from the project.
7. View the bug again.
bugs.expected_result:
The project member should be removed successfully and any bugs assigned to that user within the project should automatically become unassigned.

The bug status and other bug data should remain unchanged.
bugs.actual_result: The project member is removed successfully, but the bug remains assigned to the removed user.

bugs.title: AI Assist button is visible to Developer on New Bug form
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome 153, Desktop, Developer account, local development, branch: feat/ai-assist-access
bugs.description:
The AI Assist button is displayed on the New Bug form when the current project member has the Developer role.

REQ-018 permits AI Assist only for Project Owners and QA Analysts. Developers must not have access to the feature.

The button was intended to be hidden, but the New Bug form's general button styling overrode the HTML hidden behavior.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Sign in as a Developer who is a member of a project.
2. Open the project.
3. Open the New Bug form.
4. Observe the available form actions.
bugs.expected_result: The AI Assist button is not displayed to a Developer.
bugs.actual_result: The AI Assist button is visible on the New Bug form.

bugs.title: Whitespace-only JWT_SECRET_KEY is accepted
bugs.environment: Local development, FastAPI/Python, Isolated JWT authentication probe
bugs.description:
The application accepts a JWT_SECRET_KEY containing only whitespace.
A whitespace-only key can be used to sign and verify authentication tokens.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Use the affected pre-fix application code in an isolated test environment.
2. Set the JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable to a whitespace-only value (for example, three spaces).
3. Run an authentication probe using the JWT functionality in app/api/auth.py.
4. Attempt to generate a signed JWT using the configured whitespace-only secret.
5. Verify the generated token through the application's JWT authentication functionality.
6. Observe that the whitespace-only secret is accepted and the token can be signed and verified successfully.
bugs.expected_result: Missing, empty, or whitespace-only JWT_SECRET_KEY values should be rejected.
bugs.actual_result: Whitespace-only JWT_SECRET_KEY values are accepted and used for JWT signing and verification.

bugs.title: JWT security tests delete shared test database and cause order-dependent failures
bugs.environment: Local development, Windows 11, Python 3.14.2, pytest, FastAPI TestClient, SQLite
bugs.description:
The JWT security tests `test_missing_jwt_secret_key_raises_on_login` and `test_empty_jwt_secret_key_raises_on_login` used the shared `test_bugtriage.db` database and deleted it during their cleanup.

Because `app.database.DATABASE_NAME` was cached at module import, subsequent tests continued referencing the same database path after the file had been deleted.

This caused order-dependent test failures, including missing database tables during later authentication tests.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Use the application test suite before the JWT test-isolation fix.
2. Run the JWT security tests test_missing_jwt_secret_key_raises_on_login and test_empty_jwt_secret_key_raises_on_login.
3. Allow their original cleanup code to execute, deleting the shared test_bugtriage.db database.
4. In the same pytest process, execute a normal authentication test that uses the test_client fixture.
5. Observe that the later test continues using the cached database path but encounters missing database tables.
6. Run the affected test without the preceding JWT tests and compare the outcome.
bugs.expected_result: Each test should operate only against its intended disposable test database, independently of execution order.
bugs.actual_result:
When the JWT security tests ran before a normal authentication test, their cleanup deleted the shared test_bugtriage.db file. Subsequent tests continued using the cached database path and failed because required tables, including users, were missing.

The failures depended on test execution order.

bugs.title: Multiline AI suggestion value changes when applied to a single-line bug field
bugs.description:
When AI Assist returns a multiline suggestion for a field implemented as a single-line HTML input, the AI Suggestions panel displays the original value, but selecting Use or Use All can apply a different value to the form.

The browser removes the newline when assigning the suggestion to the single-line input. The suggestion is then removed from the pending suggestions even though the applied value differs from what the user reviewed.

Confirmed for Environment using the actual frontend with an injected, in-memory AI response during browser testing. No live AI provider response was required.

Title and Affected Version also use single-line inputs and may be affected, but this was not confirmed for those fields.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Load the New Bug form in a controlled browser test using the actual frontend.
2. Mock the AI Assist response with an Environment suggestion containing a newline: "Windows 11\nChrome 152".
3. Trigger AI Assist using the mocked response.
4. Verify that the AI Suggestions panel displays the Environment suggestion on two separate lines.
5. Click Use for the Environment suggestion.
6. Inspect the resulting Environment input value.
7. Observe that the newline has been removed and the suggestion is no longer pending.
bugs.expected_result:
The value applied to the form should match the suggestion that was presented to the user for review, or the suggestion should be rejected/normalized before it is presented as a usable suggestion.

The system should not silently change the reviewed suggestion during Use or Use All.
bugs.actual_result:
The AI Suggestions panel displays the original value containing a newline: `Windows 11\nChrome 152`.

After clicking Use, the single-line Environment input contains `Windows 11Chrome 152`.

The newline has been removed, but the suggestion is treated as successfully applied and disappears from the pending suggestions.

bugs.title: Late Create or Save response can discard a reopened bug form and newer AI suggestions
bugs.description:
A Create or Save request that was started in an older form session can still modify the UI after the user has cancelled that session and opened a new one.

If the original Create/Save response is delayed, the user can cancel and reopen the form, enter new values, and obtain new AI suggestions. When the older request eventually succeeds, its success handler acts on the newer session.

For New Bug, this can reset the newly entered form values. For New Bug and Edit Bug, it can hide the reopened form and discard the newer pending AI Suggestions state.

The underlying delayed-submission race predates REQ-020, but the REQ-020 cleanup now also causes the newer AI suggestion session to be discarded.

Investigation evidence: Reproduced in controlled browser tests for both New Bug Create and Edit Bug Save. The correction introduced session/request identity checks to prevent responses from abandoned form sessions from modifying newer sessions. Regression verification included delayed response completion scenarios.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
Precondition: Use the affected pre-fix frontend in a controlled browser test that can delay completion of Create and Save requests.

New Bug:
1. Open the New Bug form and enter valid bug information.
2. Click Create and hold the original request's response pending.
3. Cancel the form and open New Bug again.
4. Enter different bug information.
5. Trigger AI Assist and obtain new pending suggestions.
6. Release the original Create response and allow its success handler to complete.
7. Observe the state of the reopened form and its pending suggestions.

Edit Bug:
8. Open an existing bug in Edit mode and modify its fields.
9. Click Save and hold the original request's response pending.
10. Cancel editing, reopen Edit mode and enter different values.
11. Trigger AI Assist and obtain new pending suggestions.
12. Release the original Save response and allow its success handler to complete.
13. Observe the state of the reopened Edit form and its pending suggestions.
bugs.expected_result:
A response belonging to an abandoned form session should not modify the state of a newer form session.

The newer form should remain open, its current values should remain intact, and its pending AI suggestions should remain available.
bugs.actual_result:
The older successful Create/Save response acts on the newer session.

Depending on the form:
- the reopened form is hidden
- pending AI suggestions are discarded
- New Bug values can be reset
- the user's newer work is lost from the UI

bugs.title: Stale Create response can overwrite feedback in a newer bug form session
bugs.description:
A Create request from an abandoned New Bug form session can still overwrite feedback belonging to a newer reopened form session.

If an older Create succeeds after the user has cancelled and reopened the form, the application refreshes the bug list. If that refresh fails, loadBugs() writes its error to the shared bug message area without checking whether the message belongs to the current form session.

As a result, feedback from a newer user action can be replaced by an unrelated error generated by an older request.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open New Bug and enter valid data.
2. Click Create and delay the response.
3. Cancel the form.
4. Reopen New Bug.
5. Trigger a validation error in the new session, for example submit a blank title.
6. Verify the current message says Title must not be blank.
7. Allow the original Create request to complete successfully.
8. Make the bug-list refresh triggered by that stale success fail.
9. Observe the message shown for the newer form session.
bugs.expected_result:
A stale request or any follow-up operation caused by that stale request must not overwrite feedback belonging to the newer form session.

The newer validation message should remain unchanged.
bugs.actual_result:
The newer validation message is replaced by:
Unable to load bug list.

The newer form values and pending AI suggestions remain intact, but its feedback is overwritten.

bugs.title: Bug list refresh error is hidden after successful New Bug creation
bugs.description: After a normal successful New Bug creation, the form session is invalidated during cleanup before the subsequent bug-list refresh occurs. The refresh then incorrectly treats the just-completed current submission as stale and suppresses its error feedback. If refreshing the bug list fails, the user receives no indication that the displayed list may be out of date.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the New Bug form.
2. Enter valid bug data.
3. Click Create.
4. Allow the bug creation request to succeed.
5. Simulate HTTP 503 for the subsequent bug-list GET request.
6. Observe the feedback displayed after creation.
bugs.expected_result: The bug is created successfully, and if the subsequent bug-list refresh fails, the user is shown the normal bug-list error message, such as "Unable to load bug list."
bugs.actual_result: The bug is created successfully, but the bug-list refresh failure is silently suppressed and no error message is shown.

bugs.title: Delayed bug-list refresh can overwrite feedback from a newer New Bug session
bugs.description:
After a successful New Bug creation, the application starts a bug-list refresh. If that refresh is delayed and the user opens a new New Bug session before it completes, an error from the older refresh can overwrite feedback belonging to the newer form session.

The originating Create was current when the refresh started, but the refresh becomes stale while it is still in progress.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the New Bug form.
2. Enter valid bug data.
3. Click Create.
4. Allow the Create request to succeed normally.
5. Delay the subsequent bug-list refresh response or its JSON processing.
6. Open the New Bug form again.
7. In the newly opened form, trigger validation feedback such as "Title must not be blank."
8. Allow the earlier bug-list refresh to complete with an error.
9. Observe the feedback shown for the newer New Bug form.
bugs.expected_result: The newer New Bug session retains its validation feedback. The delayed refresh belonging to the previous completed Create must not modify feedback belonging to the newer form session.
bugs.actual_result: The newer validation feedback is overwritten by "Unable to load bug list." when the delayed refresh from the previous Create finishes.

bugs.title: Bug list sorting resets to Last Updated after navigating away and returning
bugs.description: The selected bug-list sort order is not preserved when the user navigates away from the project bug list and then returns.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open a project containing multiple bugs.
2. Change the bug-list sorting from Last Updated to another option.
3. Either:
   a. Open an individual bug and then return to the project, or
   b. Navigate to the Projects page and then return to the project.
4. Observe the selected sort option and bug order.
bugs.expected_result: The previously selected sorting option and corresponding bug order remain active when returning to the project during the same session.
bugs.actual_result: The sorting resets to Last Updated.

bugs.title: POST /projects returns HTTP 500 when project name is not a string
bugs.description: Project creation does not validate the type of the name field before calling string methods on it. An authenticated request with a truthy non-string name causes an unhandled AttributeError.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open Postman.
2. Create a new POST request to:
   http://127.0.0.1:8000/projects
3. In Authorization, select Bearer Token and enter the token obtained after logging in.
4. Open Body → raw → JSON.
5. Enter:
   {
     "name": 123
   }
6. Click Send.
7. Observe the response.
bugs.expected_result: The API rejects the invalid project name with a controlled validation response, such as HTTP 422, and no project is created.
bugs.actual_result:
The API returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

No project is created or saved when the error occurs.

bugs.title: Lifecycle action buttons remain enabled when required selections are missing
bugs.description:
Move to Open and Move to Development buttons remain enabled even when the selections required for the transition have not been made.

This is inconsistent with other lifecycle actions such as Send to Testing and Close, which remain disabled until their required selections are provided.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open a bug in Triage.
2. Leave the required assignee selection empty.
3. Observe the Move to Open button.
4. Click Move to Open.
5. Move a bug to the state where Move to Development is available.
6. Leave its required selection empty.
7. Observe the Move to Development button.
8. Click Move to Development.
bugs.expected_result:
Lifecycle action buttons should remain disabled until all selections required for the transition are complete.

Move to Open and Move to Development should behave consistently with Send to Testing and Close.
bugs.actual_result:
Move to Open and Move to Development remain enabled before the required selection is made.

Clicking them displays a validation message instead of preventing the action through the disabled button state.

bugs.title: Concurrent bug deletion can cause edit or status update to fail during response readback
bugs.description:
A source review identified a concurrency race in the bug edit and lifecycle/status update flows. Both handlers commit their database update before reading the bug row again to build the API response. If another authorized request deletes the same bug after the update commits but before the response SELECT executes, the readback may return no row. The handler can then attempt to access fields on the missing row and return an unexpected server error. 

Initially identified through source review. The failure was subsequently reproduced with deterministic API regression tests that simulate deletion after the database update commits but before response readback.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Create a bug in a project.
2. Start an authorized edit or lifecycle/status update request for that bug.
3. Using a controlled concurrency test, delete the bug after the update commits but before the handler performs its response readback.
4. Allow the original request to continue.
5. Observe the unexpected server error when the handler attempts to access the missing bug row.
bugs.expected_result: The request should complete with a controlled response. If the bug is deleted concurrently before response readback, the API should handle the missing resource safely and must not return an unexpected server error.
bugs.actual_result:
Before the fix, deterministic API regression tests reproduced the concurrency defect by simulating deletion of a bug after an edit or lifecycle/status update committed but before its response readback.

The subsequent readback returned no bug row, causing the affected handler to attempt to access fields on a missing row and produce an unexpected server error.

The defect was reproduced through controlled API testing rather than manual browser testing.

bugs.title: Bug action buttons shift vertically when feedback message appears
bugs.description:
When transient feedback is displayed after a bug lifecycle action, the feedback message appears above the bug action controls. Because the message occupies space in the normal document flow, the controls below it shift vertically when the message appears and shift back when it disappears.

This causes unnecessary layout movement during bug lifecycle actions.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open an existing bug.
2. Perform a valid lifecycle transition, for example move the bug to Triage.
3. Observe the action controls when the success feedback message appears.
4. Compare their position before and after the feedback message is displayed.
bugs.expected_result:
The feedback message is displayed below the relevant action controls.

The action buttons remain in the same position when transient success or error feedback appears or disappears.
bugs.actual_result: The feedback message, for example: "Bug moved to Triage." appears above the action controls and pushes them downward. When the message disappears, the controls move back upward.

bugs.title: Stale success messages persist across bug and member workflows
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in and open a project where you can manage members and create bugs.
2. Open Add Member and successfully add a new project member.
3. Verify that the member creation success message appears.
4. Click New Bug and observe whether the previous member success message remains visible.
5. Create a valid bug and verify that the bug creation success message appears.
6. Click Add Member and observe whether the previous bug creation success message remains visible.
7. Reopen New Bug and check whether the success message from the previous bug creation is still displayed.
bugs.expected_result:
Transient feedback should relate to the user's current workflow.

When the user begins another top-level action such as New Bug or Add Member, stale success/error feedback from a previous completed workflow should be cleared.

A previous bug-creation message should not remain visible during member management, and a previous member-management message should not remain visible during bug creation.
bugs.actual_result:
Previously displayed success messages remain visible after the user moves to another workflow.

For example, both of the following messages can appear simultaneously:
- Member "qa@example.com" (QA Analyst) added successfully.
- BUG-26 "Login doesn't work" created successfully.

bugs.title: Fix Version is available when creating or editing unresolved bugs
bugs.description:
The Fix Version field is currently available on the New Bug form, even though a newly reported bug has not yet been fixed.

Fix Version should represent the actual version containing a completed fix, not a planned or assumed version.

The field's visibility and editability should depend on the bug's lifecycle state. The backend should enforce the same rules to prevent invalid values being submitted directly through the API.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the AI QA Bug Triage application.
2. Open a project where you have permission to create bugs.
3. Navigate to the project's Bugs page.
4. Click the "New Bug" button.
5. Observe the fields displayed on the New Bug form.
6. Locate the "Fix Version" field.
7. Verify that the field is displayed even though the bug has not yet been created or fixed.
bugs.expected_result:
Fix Version is hidden when creating a new bug.

Fix Version is hidden and cannot be assigned when editing bugs in Triage, Open, Development or Testing.

An optional Fix Version can be entered when Testing passes and the bug is closed as Fixed.

Fix Version is visible and editable on Closed bugs with resolution Fixed.

Closed bugs with other resolutions must not retain a Fix Version.

Reopening a Closed bug clears both Resolution and Fix Version.

Backend validation enforces these restrictions.
bugs.actual_result: The New Bug form displays the Fix Version field before the bug has been fixed. The field is not restricted according to the agreed lifecycle rules.

bugs.title: Lifecycle action controls move out of view after bug status transitions
bugs.description:
When moving a bug through its lifecycle, the available action controls change depending on the current status.

Because the Bug Details section and lifecycle action area change in height and position, the newly available controls can move below the visible portion of the page.

The user must manually scroll down to locate the next lifecycle action, interrupting the workflow.

This is particularly noticeable when moving between Development and Testing, where the available action buttons and selection fields change.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the AI QA Bug Triage application.
2. Open a project containing a bug in Triage.
3. Open the bug's Details page.
4. Scroll down to the lifecycle action controls.
5. Select any required assignee and click Move to Open.
6. Continue moving the bug through Development and Testing, selecting the required assignees.
7. After each successful transition, observe the position of the newly displayed lifecycle controls.
8. Notice when the next available controls are below the visible portion of the page and require additional manual scrolling.
bugs.expected_result:
After a successful lifecycle transition, the page should automatically scroll to the bottom so the updated lifecycle controls and feedback remain visible.

The user should be able to continue the next lifecycle action without manually scrolling again.

Automatic scrolling should not occur when initially opening a bug or when a transition fails.
bugs.actual_result:
After a successful lifecycle transition, the available action controls change, but the page does not consistently adjust the scroll position.

Depending on the current status and the number of displayed controls, some actions appear below the visible portion of the page.

The user must manually scroll down to find and interact with the next lifecycle controls.

bugs.title: Original text field does not expand to use available space beside a taller AI suggestion panel
bugs.description:
When AI Assist provides a suggestion for a multiline field, the suggestion panel can become significantly taller than the original textarea displayed beside it.

The original textarea retains its normal height, even when substantial unused vertical space is available below it within the same side-by-side layout.

As a result, users must scroll inside the original textarea to read content that could otherwise be displayed using the available space. This makes comparing the original content with the AI suggestion less convenient.

Observed in the Steps to Reproduce field.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the AI QA Bug Triage application.
2. Open a project containing an existing bug report.
3. Open the bug's Details page and enter edit mode.
4. Ensure the Steps to Reproduce field contains enough text to require scrolling at its normal height.
5. Use AI Assist to generate a suggestion for Steps to Reproduce.
6. When the suggestion appears beside the original field, observe the heights of the textarea and AI suggestion panel.
7. Notice whether the original textarea expands into the available space beneath it.
bugs.expected_result:
When an AI suggestion is displayed beside a multiline original field, the original textarea should expand to use the available vertical space.

The textarea should be at least as tall as its normal height and should approximately match the AI suggestion panel's height when that panel is taller.

If the original text exceeds the expanded textarea's height, the textarea should remain independently scrollable.

When the AI suggestion is dismissed, the original textarea should return to its normal height.

The behavior should remain usable on narrower screens.
bugs.actual_result:
The original Steps to Reproduce textarea retains its shorter height while the adjacent AI Suggestion panel extends significantly farther down the page.

A large unused area remains beneath the original textarea, even though its content is long enough to require an internal scrollbar.

The user must scroll inside the original textarea to read the remaining text instead of benefiting from the available vertical space.

bugs.title: Dropdown arrow color changes based on selected value
bugs.description:
Dropdown arrows are not styled consistently across the application.

When a value is selected, some dropdown arrows inherit the selected text color. For example, selecting Blocker in the Severity field makes the arrow red, while selecting a user in an Assignee dropdown can change the arrow from muted grey-blue to white.

The arrow serves the same interactive purpose regardless of the selected value, so its appearance should remain consistent across all dropdowns.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open a New Bug form.
2. Select Blocker in the Severity dropdown.
3. Observe that the dropdown arrow changes from muted grey-blue to red.
bugs.expected_result:
All dropdown arrows should consistently use the application's muted grey-blue color, regardless of the selected value.

Selected text should retain its appropriate styling, including semantic Severity and Priority colors, while dropdown arrows remain visually neutral.

The behavior should be consistent across application pages and forms, including lifecycle controls.
bugs.actual_result:
Dropdown arrows inherit the selected text color in some fields.

For example, selecting Blocker causes the Severity dropdown arrow to appear red. In other dropdowns, the arrow can change from muted grey-blue to white after a selection is made.

This creates inconsistent visual styling across otherwise similar controls.

bugs.title: Unexpected black background bar behind AI Priority suggestion "Urgent"
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn; dark mode; Futuristic QA theme enabled through UI theme lab
bugs.description:
When reviewing AI-generated suggestions on the bug editing page, a dark rectangular bar appears behind the suggested Priority value "Urgent".

The bar extends across most of the suggestion card's content area and looks inconsistent with the styling of other AI suggestion cards.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the AI QA Bug Triage application.
2. Open a project containing a bug report.
3. Open the bug for editing.
4. Enable the Futuristic QA theme through the UI theme lab.
5. Request AI-assisted triage or open a bug with pending AI suggestions.
6. Locate an AI Priority suggestion with the value "Urgent".
7. Observe the appearance of the suggested value.
bugs.expected_result: The suggested Priority value "Urgent" is displayed clearly, with its intended text color and consistent styling. No unexpected dark bar appears behind the text.
bugs.actual_result: A dark, nearly black rectangular bar appears behind "Urgent" and extends horizontally across most of the AI suggestion card.

bugs.title: Incomplete horizontal dividers in bug details when Fix Version and Resolution are hidden
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn; dark mode; Futuristic QA theme enabled through the temporary Chrome DevTools theme lab.
bugs.description:
On the read-only Bug Details page, horizontal separator lines below the Assignee and Status sections extend only approximately halfway across the details container when Fix Version and Resolution are not displayed.

This creates an inconsistent appearance compared with other full-width section dividers.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
Preconditions:
A bug exists in the Triage state, with Fix Version and Resolution not currently applicable or displayed.

1. Log in to the AI QA Bug Triage application.
2. Open a project containing a bug report in the Triage state.
3. Open the read-only details page for that bug (for example, BUG-38).
4. Scroll to the bottom metadata section containing Assignee, Status, Created, and Updated.
5. Observe the horizontal separator lines below Assignee and Status.
bugs.expected_result:
When Fix Version and Resolution are not displayed, horizontal dividers beneath Assignee and Status extend across the entire width of the details container, consistent with other section dividers.

The positioning of the existing fields must remain unchanged.

When Fix Version and Resolution become applicable and visible, the layout should continue to display correctly.
bugs.actual_result: The divider lines below Assignee and Status extend only across the left half of the details container, leaving the right half visually empty.

bugs.title: Double turquoise border appears when focusing form fields
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn; dark mode; Futuristic Refined — Vivid Colors theme enabled through the temporary Chrome DevTools theme lab.
bugs.description:
When hovering over an editable form field, its border changes to turquoise as intended. However, clicking inside the field adds a second solid turquoise outline outside the existing border.

This creates an unnecessarily thick, double-border appearance. The issue affects the visual consistency of form controls but does not prevent users from entering or saving data.

The issue has been observed on the Bug Edit page, particularly with textareas and dropdowns.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to AI QA Bug Triage.
2. Open a project containing an existing bug.
3. Open the bug details page and click "Edit".
4. Hover over the "Actual Result" textarea and observe the turquoise border.
5. Click inside the textarea while keeping the mouse pointer over it.
6. Observe the double turquoise border.
7. Repeat with the "Assignee" dropdown.
bugs.expected_result: Hovering over a field highlights its border in turquoise. When the field receives focus, a single clear turquoise border should be displayed, optionally with a subtle glow. Hover and focus effects should not produce overlapping solid outlines. Keyboard focus must remain clearly visible.
bugs.actual_result: When a field receives focus, a second turquoise outline appears outside the existing highlighted border, resulting in two visible concentric lines around the field.

bugs.title: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast failure for Blocker/Urgent text in dark theme
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn; dark mode; Futuristic Refined — Vivid Colors theme enabled through the temporary Chrome DevTools theme lab.
bugs.description:
The Blocker severity and Urgent priority labels do not meet WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.3 — Contrast (Minimum), Level AA, when displayed against the brighter backgrounds of the Bug List and read-only Bug Details page.

The original text color #FF1744 provides approximately 3.3–3.7:1 contrast, depending on the background and hover state. The minimum required ratio is 4.5:1 because the labels are 16px text.

This may reduce readability for users with low vision or reduced contrast sensitivity.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Enable the Futuristic Refined — Vivid Colors dark theme.
2. Open a project containing a bug with Severity = Blocker and Priority = Urgent.
3. Locate the bug in the Bug List.
4. Observe the Blocker/Urgent text in normal and hovered row states.
5. Open the bug's read-only Bug Details page.
6. Measure the foreground/background contrast using a WCAG contrast checker.
bugs.expected_result: All severity and priority values meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA contrast requirements, including normal and hover states. Normal-sized text must achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast.
bugs.actual_result:
Bug List normal background (#1B2D46): approximately 3.61:1.

Bug List brighter hover background (previously measured): approximately 3.32:1.

Bug Details including gradient: approximately 3.61–3.68:1.

All labels are 16px and do not qualify for the large-text exception.

bugs.title: Bug List table does not fit mobile viewport, requiring horizontal scrolling to access bug information
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn; mobile viewport emulated using Chrome DevTools.
bugs.description:
On narrow mobile viewports, the Bug List retains a desktop-oriented table layout that exceeds the available screen width. As a result, only the first columns are visible, while additional bug information is positioned outside the viewport.

Users must scroll horizontally to access the remaining columns, making it difficult to scan, compare, and navigate bug reports on mobile devices.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the application.
2. Open a project containing multiple bug reports.
3. Set the browser viewport width to 390px using Chrome DevTools.
4. Navigate to the Bug List.
5. Observe the table layout and attempt to access the columns outside the visible area.
bugs.expected_result:
The Bug List should adapt to narrow mobile viewports, presenting bug information in a readable and usable responsive layout.

Important bug details and available actions should be easily accessible without requiring users to navigate a desktop-width table.

The layout should maintain appropriate text wrapping, spacing, and touch-friendly interactive elements.
bugs.actual_result:
The Bug List retains a desktop-width table layout that exceeds the available mobile viewport width.

Only the initial columns, including Bug ID, Title, and Severity, are visible without horizontal scrolling. Additional columns extend beyond the visible area.

Users must scroll horizontally to access the remaining information, making it difficult to scan and compare bug reports.

bugs.title: AI suggestion validation accepts conflicting duplicate JSON properties
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Python 3.14.2, FastAPI backend, OpenAI API adapter (mocked provider response)
bugs.description:
The AI-assisted triage backend accepts a malformed AI response containing duplicate JSON object properties with conflicting values.

Python's default JSON decoder silently retains the last occurrence of a duplicate property. Consequently, the AI suggestion validator never receives both values and cannot detect the conflict.

This violates the intended AI output validation behavior under AC-019.3 and AC-019.4.

The issue was reproduced using a mocked provider response. No occurrence was confirmed with the live OpenAI API.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Prepare an AI-assisted triage request using a mocked OpenAI provider response.
2. Configure the mock to return a suggestion containing duplicate JSON properties with conflicting values, for example:
   {"field":"title","value":"First","value":"Second"}
3. Pass the mocked response through the application's OpenAI response adapter and AI suggestion validation pipeline.
4. Inspect the parsed response and resulting validated suggestion.
5. Observe which Title value is accepted.
bugs.expected_result:
The backend detects duplicate JSON object properties and rejects the ambiguous AI response before domain validation.

No suggestion derived from the malformed response is presented as usable. Existing AI failure handling preserves the user's form data and allows manual continuation or retry.
bugs.actual_result:
Python's JSON decoder silently discards the first value and retains the last value ("Second").

The AI suggestion validator receives only the retained value and accepts it as a usable Title suggestion.

The conflicting duplicate properties are not detected.

bugs.title: Success message overflows the viewport when creating a bug with an extremely long title
bugs.description:
When creating a bug with an extremely long title, the success confirmation message displays the entire bug title without properly constraining or wrapping the text.

As a result, the message extends beyond the page's content area and is clipped at the right edge of the viewport.

The bug title itself is displayed correctly in the bug list and bug details page. The issue is limited to the success confirmation message.

This is a minor UI presentation defect and does not prevent successful bug creation.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in as a Project Owner.
2. Open an existing project.
3. Click "New Bug".
4. Enter an extremely long title consisting of repeated characters (e.g., several hundred characters without spaces).
5. Complete the other required fields.
6. Click "Create".
7. Observe the success confirmation message above the bug list.
bugs.expected_result:
The success confirmation message should remain within the page boundaries and be fully readable, regardless of the bug title's length.

Long text should wrap, be truncated appropriately, or be omitted from the confirmation message.
bugs.actual_result:
The bug is created successfully, but the confirmation message includes the entire extremely long title.

The message extends horizontally beyond the page content area and is clipped at the right edge of the viewport.

The title displays correctly in the bug list and bug details page.

bugs.title: AI Assist does not use relevant historical bug data in suggestions
bugs.environment: Windows 11, GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI API, Python evaluation harness)
bugs.description:
During real-model evaluation of AC-019.2, AI Assist generated valid suggestions but did not demonstrate use of relevant historical bug information.

In scenario EVAL-D (TC-354), two closely related historical bugs contained matching Environment, Affected Version, Severity, Priority and Assignee values.

Across two independent GPT-6 Luna evaluations, AI Assist only rewrote information already present in the current bug report. None of the distinctive historical values appeared in the suggestions.

Reproduced in 2/2 evaluation runs.

This is a suspected AI suggestion-quality issue. Further investigation is needed to determine whether the behavior results from overly conservative prompting or is acceptable under the current requirements.

Evidence (stored locally):
Pass 1: ai-evaluation-results/20261016T130306Z-a7300483/run.json
Pass 2: ai-evaluation-results/20261016T131919Z-625454ca/run.json
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open the AI evaluation scenario EVAL-D (TC-354).
2. Use the fictional current bug "Export stays disabled for an empty grid", leaving Environment, Affected Version, Severity, Priority and Assignee unspecified.
3. Include historical bugs 501 and 502, both containing Environment "TestOS 4 / Aster Browser 12", Affected Version "0.8.2", Severity "Moderate", Priority "Medium" and Assignee ID 12.
4. Run the real-model evaluation using GPT-6 Luna with the existing production prompt and response validation.
5. Inspect the generated suggestions for Scenario D.
6. Repeat the evaluation with the same scenario inputs.
7. Compare both responses against the current bug and historical data.
bugs.expected_result: AI Assist considers relevant historical reports when generating suggestions. Where reasonably supported, it may suggest missing field values or other useful improvements derived from that history without presenting historical information as independently verified facts about the current bug.
bugs.actual_result:
Across two real-model evaluation runs, AI Assist generated valid suggestions that only rewrote existing current-bug information.

Neither response suggested any distinctive values from the two relevant historical bugs, including Environment, Affected Version, Severity, Priority or Assignee.

Historical-context usefulness was therefore not demonstrated. No factual fabrication or invalid response was observed.

bugs.title: Globally sequential project IDs expose internal project numbering
bugs.description:
Project URLs expose globally sequential database IDs. When a newly registered user creates their first project, the URL may contain a relatively high project ID (e.g., /project.html?id=30), revealing information about the application's global project numbering.

Although this does not expose other users' project contents or establish how many projects currently exist, it unnecessarily discloses internal identifier allocation.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Register a new user account and log in.
2. Create the user's first project.
3. Open the newly created project.
4. Observe the browser URL (e.g., /project.html?id=30).
5. Notice that the project ID reflects global project numbering rather than an identifier specific to the new user's activity.
bugs.expected_result: Public-facing project URLs should use opaque, non-sequential identifiers that do not expose global project numbering. Internal numeric database IDs may remain unchanged.
bugs.actual_result: The browser URL exposes the globally sequential numeric project ID (e.g., /project.html?id=30), allowing users to infer that other project IDs have previously been allocated.

bugs.title: New Bug form allows multiple submissions and creates duplicate reports
bugs.description: The New Bug form allows repeated submissions while the initial Create request is still pending. Multiple POST requests are processed, resulting in duplicate bug reports being saved from a single intended creation workflow.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Open a project and click New Bug.
2. Open Chrome DevTools (F12), go to Network and enable Slow 4G throttling.
3. Enter some title for the bug.
4. Click **Create** repeatedly while the request is pending.
5. Check the bug list for duplicate reports.
bugs.expected_result: Only one bug report should be created per submission. The Create button should be disabled while the request is pending to prevent duplicate submissions. It should become available again if the request fails.
bugs.actual_result:
Multiple bug reports were created from repeated clicks on Create. During manual reproduction, eight separate reports (BUG-1 through BUG-8), all titled "Aaa1", were created within approximately two seconds.

Each report received a unique bug ID, confirming that duplicate submissions were processed and persisted.

The defect was reproduced using Chrome DevTools with 3G network throttling.

bugs.title: Adding a project member with an invalid email type returns HTTP 500
bugs.description: The Add Member API does not properly validate the email field when it contains a non-string value. Sending an array instead of an email string results in HTTP 500 Internal Server Error instead of a validation error.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Start the isolated Postman test server.
2. Authenticate as a Project Owner.
3. Send POST /projects/{project_id}/members with the following JSON body:
   {"email": ["qa@example.com"], "role": "Developer"}
4. Check the response status.
bugs.expected_result: The API rejects the invalid email type with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. No project membership is created.
bugs.actual_result: The API returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when the email field contains an array instead of a string.

bugs.title: Inconsistent font family across application pages
bugs.description: Some application text uses the browser-default serif font instead of Arial, causing inconsistent typography across pages and form controls.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in to the application.
2. Open a project and select Create Bug.
3. Compare form labels with input text and buttons.
4. Open the About page and compare its text with navigation and headings.
bugs.expected_result: Application text and form controls use consistent Arial typography, except intentionally styled elements such as AI suggestions.
bugs.actual_result: Form labels and other text appear in a serif font, while headings, inputs and some navigation elements use Arial.

bugs.title: Bug List pagination controls shift vertically between pages with different title lengths
bugs.description:
The Bug List's Previous/Next pagination controls change their vertical position when navigating between full pages containing bug reports with different title lengths.

Longer titles cause table rows to expand, while shorter titles produce a shorter table. Because pagination controls are positioned beneath the table, these height differences cause the controls to move vertically, making repeated navigation inconvenient.

Note that pagination controls may still change position on the last page when it contains fewer bugs than the selected page size. This is expected and acceptable because the table naturally contains fewer rows. It is outside the scope of this defect.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in and open a project containing multiple full pages of bug reports with varying title lengths.
2. Set Bugs per page to 10.
3. Navigate to a full page containing mostly short bug titles.
4. Note the vertical position of the Previous/Next pagination controls.
5. Navigate to another full page containing longer bug titles.
6. Observe that the pagination controls have moved vertically.
7. Navigate back and forth between these pages and observe the repeated position changes.
bugs.expected_result:
Pagination controls should maintain a consistent vertical position when navigating between full pages containing the same number of bugs, regardless of title length.

Users should be able to navigate repeatedly without having to reposition the pointer or scroll to locate the controls.
bugs.actual_result:
The height of the Bug List varies depending on how many lines bug titles occupy.

Consequently, the Previous/Next controls shift vertically when navigating between full pages containing different title lengths, making repeated navigation inconvenient.

bugs.title: Bug List background brightness changes with different Bugs per page settings
bugs.environment: Windows 11, Chrome, FastAPI/Uvicorn, desktop/mobile viewports, dark/light themes
bugs.description:
The page background glow changes brightness when switching between 10, 20 and 50 bugs per page. The difference is most noticeable near the top centre of the page, particularly in dark mode.

The issue occurs because the body's radial-gradient background scales with the full document height instead of the viewport height. Displaying more bugs increases the document height, stretching the gradient and changing its appearance.
bugs.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Log in and open a project containing at least 50 bug reports.
2. Enable dark mode and scroll to the top of the page.
3. Set Bugs per page to 10 and observe the background glow near the top centre.
4. Change Bugs per page to 50 without changing the viewport size.
5. Compare the background brightness.
6. Repeat with 20 bugs per page and in light mode.
bugs.expected_result: The background glow should maintain consistent brightness and positioning regardless of the number of bugs displayed per page. Changing pagination settings should not alter the page's background appearance.
bugs.actual_result: Increasing Bugs per page stretches the background gradient, making the glow brighter near the top centre. The appearance changes even when the viewport size, theme and scroll position remain unchanged.
